decision.title: Part registries and the evaluator seams (packet )

item.p: Library parts by glob. cmake/SxmlParts.cmake reads every src/function_library_*.c and generates function_library_parts.c in the build tree from each definition const sxml_native_function_view sxml_function_library_<part> =; files without one (case tables, deep equality, function_library.c) are not parts. A part serves every language unless it also defines const sxml_language_set sxml_function_library_<part>_languages = SXML_LANGUAGE_XSLT; (any of SXML_LANGUAGE_XPATH, _XQUERY, _XSLT joined by |): CMake reads the names, the generated table also points at the variable, and a unit test checks the two agree. src/function_library_parts_internal.h declares sxml_function_library_registered_parts() (every part, sorted by name) and sxml_function_library_parts_for_language() (a static list per language). The processor and the fuzz fixture take the XPath list; XQuery and XSLT compilation take theirs (3.x, 4.x). A new part declares its own extern view (or none: the generated unit declares it); function_library_internal.h keeps the Phase 1 declarations.

Evaluator parts by glob. The same module reads src/evaluator_*.c for const sxml_evaluator_part sxml_evaluator_part_<part> =: a table of IR expression kinds and step functions. The machine runs its built-in kinds itself and every other kind through the registry; a kind no part claims, or two parts claim, is SXML_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE (a unit test checks each reserved kind has exactly one). Parts construct (seven constructors, SHALLOW_COPY), try (TRY_CATCH), template (APPLY_TEMPLATES) and global (no kind; sxml_evaluator_start_global_initializers, called before the main function's body runs for globals with an initializer and no value) return UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE until 3.5, 3.6, 4.x and 3.10 fill them. A given value of a global with an initializer wins (an external variable's default). 3.10's reads on demand need the reading task to wait for the initializer; if the global part cannot do it with tasks pushed at the start (in dependency order), 3.10 proposes a machine change.

A part is live when its file is: a committed part file joins every build, the processor and the fuzz fixture at once, so its rows must not repeat a name and arity another part serves (the library then refuses to start, INVALID_ARGUMENT); a packet moving rows moves them in one commit.

Machine API in src/evaluator_machine_internal.h (defined in src/evaluator.c): the task type, top task, push an expression task in the top task's frame, push a part task (a step function and owned state with its release function), hand a value down (finish), take the value of the task above, read and bind atoms, raise (report into the error record), and catching: a task whose catches_errors is set receives a dynamic or type error raised above it. The run loop locates the error, unwinds every task above the innermost catching task above its base, stores the status in the context (caught_status) and steps that task again; limits, memory and invalid-argument statuses are never caught. No C recursion: step functions return to the one loop ().

Rejected: a hand-kept part list (every new part edits the processor, the fuzz fixture and tests: 's conflict); per-language libraries chosen at run time from flags in the view (needs a change of the frozen row header and filtering memory).
